title: Why Activating Brown Fat to Treat Obesity is So Hard - Nautilus
gist: Teaser for a piece on why activating brown fat as an obesity treatment has proven difficult; the captured text contains only an opening joke about publication bias ('No one publishes negative data'), setting up an argument that failed results matter.

insights.claim: Negative results in research often go unpublished, causing others to repeat the same failed approaches—framed as the key lesson for brown-fat obesity research.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Publication bias hides failure rates, so investors in metabolic-drug pipelines should discount early mechanism hype.
insights.quote: “No one publishes negative data,” the PhD student replies.

insights.claim: Activating brown fat to treat obesity has proven hard, and the author argues the failures carry as much value as successes.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Brown-fat activation remains an unproven obesity mechanism compared with other approaches.
insights.locator: Why Activating Brown Fat to Treat Obesity is So Hard
